subtype: Approach: check safety and call emergency services first [Action]
passage:
Note to file, written the evening of the crash.

A scooter and a van collided at the junction outside the gate. Shalini, a second-year student walking ahead of me, stopped at once, stepped onto the pavement and looked back along the road before going near. Then Shalini raised a hand to slow a lorry, dialled 112 and said clearly: "One person on the road, awake, a van blocking the left lane, outside the college gate." I stayed beside the rider. Shalini went to the corner to wave the ambulance in. The police arrived soon after and took over.

Shalini's voice stayed steady on the call, but the hands were shaking afterwards. I've asked Shalini to come and see me tomorrow, just to talk.

Kishore, faculty coordinator

qa.q: What do Shalini's shaking hands suggest about how Shalini felt?
qa.a: They suggest Shalini was frightened and shaken after the event, even though the voice on the call stayed steady.

qa.q: What could Shalini and Kishore do while waiting for the ambulance, and why?
qa.a: They could ask a bystander to keep other people back and stay on the line for instructions, because trained responders can guide them and crowds add risk.

qa.q: How might the rider have experienced the minutes before help came?
qa.a: The rider probably felt scared and hurt but a little safer knowing someone stayed close and help had been called.

grounding: Illustrates a young bystander first checking for traffic danger, moving to a safe spot and calling the emergency number.

subtype: Approach: check safety and call emergency services first [Action]
passage:
Tuesday night.
Still shaky. On the way back from coaching, a scooter hit a car at the Ring Road signal right in front of me. The rider was on the ground and not getting up.
I wanted to run to him. Instead I did what the poster at college says. First I stepped back onto the footpath, away from the traffic. Then I looked: cars still coming in the second lane, petrol smell, rider not moving. I didn't go near the road.
I called 112 and said exactly where: Ring Road, near the petrol pump signal, one rider down, not moving, car driver standing. They said an ambulance and police were coming. I stayed on the footpath and waved when I saw the ambulance.
Anjali called me after I texted her. She said I did the right thing by calling first.
I keep seeing it when I close my eyes. I'm going to talk to Ammi about it tomorrow.
Farhan

qa.q: How is Farhan feeling while writing the entry?
qa.a: Farhan feels shaky and upset, still seeing the crash when closing both eyes.

qa.q: What else could Farhan do after such an experience?
qa.a: Farhan could talk it through with Ammi and, if the images keep coming back, speak to a counsellor, since witnessing a crash can stay with a person.

qa.q: How might the injured rider be affected by Farhan's call?
qa.a: The rider got trained help faster because Farhan gave a clear location and details instead of stepping into traffic.

grounding: Shows a young bystander at a crash moving to safety, checking for traffic and fuel, and calling ambulance and police through the emergency number first.

passage:
Sarika: Kamal, are you home? I saw an accident near the flyover
Kamal: what?? are you ok
Sarika: I'm fine. a bike skidded and the rider fell near the divider
Kamal: did you go to him?
Sarika: not straight away. trucks were still going past. I moved behind the barrier first
Sarika: I checked if anything was leaking or burning. nothing
Sarika: then I called 112. told them the flyover exit, one rider down, conscious but not getting up
Kamal: did they come?
Sarika: ambulance in 12 minutes. police too. I stayed behind the barrier and talked to him from there, told him help was coming
Kamal: that was smart. I'd have run straight into the road
Sarika: I nearly did. my legs are still shaking
Kamal: come home. I'll make tea and you can tell Mummy properly

qa.q: How long did the ambulance take to arrive?
How is Sarika feeling after the accident?
qa.a: Sarika is shaken, with legs still shaking, after nearly running into the road and then handling it calmly.

qa.q: What else could Sarika do now that the rider is with the ambulance?
qa.a: Sarika could rest, tell the family what happened, and talk to someone if the scene keeps coming back.

qa.q: How does Kamal see what Sarika did?
qa.a: Kamal thinks it was smart and admits to being the kind who would run into the road, so Kamal is impressed and relieved Sarika is safe.

grounding: Shows a young bystander moving to safety, checking for danger and calling ambulance and police on the emergency number before anything else.
